subject.title: Feature: Global session reset on auth switch

question: Should global auth refresh preserve explicit per-session user-selected profiles and wait for safe turn boundaries, or forcibly move every active session to the newly selected credentials?
rationale: Current main deliberately preserves explicit auth pins and active-run lifecycle ownership, so automation cannot safely decide which of those security and state contracts a global operation may override.

options.title: Preserve pins and defer runs
options.body: Refresh automatic bindings at the next safe turn boundary while leaving explicit user-selected profiles unchanged and reporting skipped sessions.

options.title: Force every session immediately
options.body: Override explicit pins and interrupt active runs so all sessions adopt the newly selected credentials at once.

options.title: Keep targeted controls only
options.body: Decline a bulk mutation and instead improve diagnostics and per-session recovery for stale or pinned auth state.

recommendation.title: Preserve pins and defer runs
recommendation.body: Refresh automatic bindings at the next safe turn boundary while leaving explicit user-selected profiles unchanged and reporting skipped sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main history across the Gateway session reset and auth lifecycle surfaces and has already participated in this issue's product review.
